title: Per-tenant adapter modules and var-surface patching for private VPC deployments
creator: Nina Patel
description: Design and implement a lightweight, maintainable pattern for per-customer Terraform customizations that avoids forking upstream modules. Deliver adapter/patch modules and a var-surface patching convention that let customers express VPC-specific overrides, provider differences, and safe upgrade paths without duplicating full module implementations.
background: We repeatedly see customers needing small but divergent changes to network and infra configurations for Private (VPC) deployments: CIDR tweaks, specialized NAT/IGW configurations, vendor-specific route table settings, and regulatory tag/labeling rules. Existing approaches duplicate whole modules or maintain fragile overlays that break on upstream module upgrades. This ticket proposes a composable adapter/shim strategy plus variable-surface patching and validation to make per-customer customizations robust and upgrade-safe.
goals: Provide a documented pattern for per-tenant customizations that minimizes duplicated code
Support provider-agnostic adapters (AWS/GCP/Azure) and a clear precedence model for variable overrides
Enable automated validation and schema checks to catch breaking changes during module upgrades
Ship a reference implementation (adapter modules + test harness) and migration guide for 3 pilot customers
non_goals: Replace all existing overlay approaches immediately
Build a complete UI for tenant-level customization (console work tracked separately)
proposed_solution: Introduce a small 'tenant_adapters' layer that sits between the tenant overlay and upstream infra modules. Each adapter is a thin wrapper that translates a constrained 'tenant_vars' surface into the inputs expected by upstream modules. Provide a 'patch' convention: tenant_vars contains a top-level 'patches' list with typed patches (replace/merge/insert) and a declarative precedence order. Include a compile-time validation step (terraform validate + custom schema linter) and a migration tool that converts existing overlays into adapter patches.
design_decisions: Adapter modules are opinionated and only cover common extension points (networking, tags, peering). Complex custom modules continue to live in customer repos
Patch types limited to three operations to keep reasoning simple: merge (deep merge maps), replace (full replace), and set-path (targeted assignment)
Precedence: global defaults -> release profile -> tenant_vars.patches (applied in order) -> final tenant overrides
No dynamic eval in patches; expressions allowed only at top-level variables to avoid remote-exec-like complexity
implementation_steps: Spec: write RFC describing tenant_vars schema, patch types, and precedence rules (doc/adapter-schema-2026.md)
Implement tenant_adapters/aws and tenant_adapters/gcp modules with simple translations for 6 upstream inputs (vpc_cidr, public_subnets, nat_strategy, tags, dns_options, route_table_customizations)
Create patch-apply utility (go) that reads patches and emits a merged vars file; integrate as a pre-apply hook in CI
Add terraform schema linter rules and a 'schema_version' field to tenant_vars to support safe upgrades
Build Terratest suite that runs 3 canonical scenarios per cloud and verifies plan diffs are limited to expected resources
Write migration script to convert 5 pilot customers' overlays into adapter patches and run in a staging tenant
Document the pattern and produce a 'how-to' playbook for Solutions/SEs
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement adapters + linter and run internal tests (2 sprints). Phase 2: onboard 3 pilot customers with migration script; use canary apply with detailed drift/plan review. Phase 3: iterate on patch types based on pilot feedback and publish RFC for general availability. Rollback path: tenant_vars keep previous schema_version and adapter keeps old translation layer for 2 releases.
testing_plan: Unit tests for patch applier, Terratest plans with real provider mocks for each cloud, CI pre-apply gate that runs 'plan' and checks for unexpected resource replacements. Add a QA checklist for pilot customer applies including manual plan review by infra owner and SE.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter modules implemented for AWS and GCP with documented inputs
Patch applier utility passes unit tests and integrates into CI pre-apply pipeline
Three pilot customers successfully migrated in staging without manual module duplication
Schema linter catches at least 2 simulated upgrade-break scenarios during testing
Documentation and migration playbook published and reviewed by Solutions Engineering
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Patch semantics may be confusing and lead to subtle misconfigurations. Mitigation: Keep patch types small and provide a simulator that shows pre/post merged vars
Risk: Upstream module changes still break adapters. Mitigation: Add schema_version and adapter compatibility metadata; run compatibility tests on module upgrades
Risk: Performance/complexity of pre-apply merge for very large var sets. Mitigation: implement incremental patching and cache merged output per tenant
notes_and_comments: 2026-02-12 Nina Patel: Kickoff - drafted initial RFC and prototype adapter mapping for AWS. Raised question about whether to support provider-specific feature flags.

2026-02-18 Diego Martinez: Prototype review - adapter wrapper looks minimal. Concern: route_table_customizations shape varies a lot across customers. Suggest adding a typed 'route_template' with interpolation tokens.
2026-02-23 SE Team (Slack): Pilot candidates identified: AcmeFin, MedComms, RetailCo. AcmeFin requires strict tagging and custom NAT for compliance; MedComms uses shared services VPC patterns.
2026-02-26 QA: Added Terratest checklist and initial CI pre-apply job (internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123)
2026-02-28 Security review: confirmed that adapters do not increase Blast Radius; recommended adding explicit allowlist for any provider-level overrides (see confluence link)
2026-03-01 Diego Martinez: Updated RFC with schema_version and migration path. Marking ticket Planned for execution in next cycle
implementation_notes: Prefer small, documented changes. Keep adapters in a separate repo to allow independent release cadence. Use semantic versioning on adapter modules and require explicit opt-in of new adapter major versions per tenant.
post_mortem_plan: If a pilot migration causes drift or breaks, capture incident notes in infra-incident tracker, run revert using cached merged vars and run a postmortem with SE + infra owners within 72 hours
